title: The Tortoise and the Eagle
summary: A little creature longs to fly and begs a powerful bird for a chance.
coverScene: A small turtle looks up with excitement at a large eagle flying high above the green land.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, a small animal had a big wish to fly up.

The small animal felt that life on the ground was too slow for him.
He had always wanted to see the world from high above.
One afternoon, a strong bird landed near the small animal on the ground.
The small animal asked the big bird for help with his secret wish.
The big bird explained that animals of his kind were not made for flying.
However, the small animal would not listen to any good advice from his friend.
The big bird agreed to try and took the small animal up.
They flew high above the tall trees and the small town houses.
The small animal felt glad as the wind blew around him in the air.
He forgot that his heavy body could not support him up in the open sky.
He started to shout with extreme happiness, believing he was a bird like the others.
Suddenly, the big bird let go because the small animal moved too much.
The small animal began to fall fast toward the hard ground below.
He realized his mistake too late before a heavy crash against a large stone.
From that day on, the small animal never wanted to fly again in his life.
He has stayed on the ground and walked slowly through the green plants.
The experience has taught him that every living thing has its proper place in the world.
Many days have passed since that terrible accident happened in the open field near the town.
If the small animal tried to fly again, he would surely fall down.
Therefore, he always stays close to the safe earth and walks slowly every day.
He has learned that life on the ground is the best place for him to live.
Other animals in the area have seen what happened to him during that strange flight.
They also know that flying is only for birds in the sky.
If anyone asks the small animal about his trip, he just smiles and shakes his head.
He has never forgotten the lessons of that afternoon when he tried to reach high.
The world is full of wonderful things to see.
He does not need to leave the safety of the green trees.
Every animal must accept his own natural limits and be glad with what he has.
He will never go up into the open sky again.
The ground is his home and he will stay there for the rest of his life.
Life is good when you walk on the green earth and look at the trees.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, within the quiet valleys of a timeless land, there lived a humble tortoise who possessed an immense and restless desire to fly.
He spent every endless day watching majestic birds soar high up in the brilliant blue sky, wishing fiercely that he could join them.
The terrestrial animal felt that his life upon the solid ground was far too slow and remarkably boring.
He hungered to see the world from high above, just like the large birds did every single afternoon.
That heavy shell upon his back felt less like a protective home and more like a heavy burden anchoring him to the dust.
One particularly warm afternoon, a powerful eagle flew down from the clouds and landed near the curious creature.
Seizing the rare moment, the tortoise walked directly to the magnificent bird and politely asked for assistance.
He explained his deep, burning wish to fly across the open clouds and witness distant places that no ground-dwelling soul had ever seen.
The eagle looked down at him with genuine surprise, tilting his sharp head to study the strange petitioner.
With a cautious voice, the raptor tried to explain that tortoises were simply not made for the freedom of the air.
However, the stubborn creature would not listen to any reason or accept any good advice from his majestic visitor.
He asked the bird again and again with relentless persistence until the eagle finally agreed to try the impossible experiment.
If the tortoise had known the terrible danger awaiting him in the winds, he would have stayed firmly upon the grass.
If the eagle had not relented and helped him, the tragic fall would never have happened at all.
If the creature possessed even a shred of true wisdom, he would have remained satisfied with walking the earth.
Perched high on the sturdy branch of a tall oak tree, the wise eagle watched the tortoise prepare for his great journey.
The great bird reached down, grasped the heavy animal firmly in his strong talons, and began to rise into the air.
They swept high above the green trees, the rolling green hills, and the small, distant houses of the nearby town.
The tortoise felt an astonishing, electric sense of pure happiness as the cool wind rushed loudly around his face.
He looked down at the shrinking earth below and thought that he must be the most successful animal alive.
In that intoxicating moment of dizzying triumph, he completely forgot that he had no wings of his own.
His heavy, solid shell could not possibly support him in the thin air without the assistance of his carrier.
Overcome by sudden vanity, he started to shout with loud joy, firmly believing that he had somehow transformed into a bird.
He demanded that the eagle acknowledge his newfound status as master of the sky, gesturing wildly with his stubby legs.
Only a fool would dance upon the edge of an abyss, yet the tortoise rejoiced while dangling miles above the stones.
Suddenly, irritated by the chaotic movement and the foolish noise, the eagle abruptly let go of his clumsy passenger.
The silly creature began to fall fast through the open air, heading straight down toward the hard, unforgiving ground.
Panic replaced pride in an instant as the rush of wind turned from a sweet song into a terrifying roar.
He realized his enormous mistake far too late, wishing desperately that he had stayed safe and sound upon the earth.
Gravity reclaimed its own with ruthless efficiency, offering no mercy to the dreamer who defied the natural order.
With a loud, resounding crash that echoed across the valley, the poor creature landed squarely on a large, jagged stone.
The impact shattered his illusions entirely, teaching him a very hard, painful lesson about desire and reality.
People in the nearby town often talk about that strange afternoon when the land-bound animal tried to touch the clouds.
This dramatic story remains an important, sobering lesson for anyone who foolishly wishes for things that cannot be.
Bruised and aching, the survivor lay motionless for a long time while the quiet wind whispered through the grass.
From that exact day onward, the chastened animal never wanted to fly again, not even for a fleeting second.
He stayed permanently on the ground where he belonged, walking slowly and carefully through the green grass.
The harrowing experience taught him a profound truth: every living creature has its own proper place in the world.
He finally understood that wishing for things far beyond one natural ability only brings unnecessary trouble and grief.
No longer would he gaze upward with bitterness; instead, he accepted the quiet peace of the solid earth beneath his feet.
Every single morning, the tortoise walked slowly through the familiar meadows, feeling the reassuring texture of the soil.
He often thought about the disastrous flight that had caused him so much physical pain and emotional regret.
High above in the branches of the old trees, the great eagle would occasionally watch him from a distance.
The tortoise knew with absolute certainty that he must never leave the safety of the ground again.
His heavy, rounded shell was clearly meant for slow walking, not for soaring carelessly through the distant clouds.
Other local animals looked at him often and quietly understood the deep moral lesson hidden within his misfortune.
Life on the earth was more than good enough for everyone who lived there without chasing impossible dreams.
The story of the foolish flight was told and retold by the local villagers for many long years.
Parents shared the tale with their children to ensure they learned the value of patience and self-acceptance.
Wisdom, after all, is frequently bought through bitter experience and the sudden shattering of pride.
As the sun began to set behind the hills, casting long shadows across the peaceful valley, the tortoise found his rest.
He pulled his head safely inside his strong shell, feeling secure in the quiet twilight of the darkening world.
The sky above turned from brilliant orange to deep indigo, filled with genuine birds returning to their nests.
He felt no envy toward them now, only a quiet respect for the natural boundaries that kept them all safe.
Some dreams are better left unfulfilled, and some journeys are best measured by the wisdom of return.
